item.subject: Mathematics
item.stem:
The graph shows the distribution of crops grown in a certain country.

[Image: Pie chart showing the distribution of crops]

According to the information in the graph, which of these statements is true?

options.label: A
options.text: More oats are grown than wheat.

options.label: B
options.text: Corn is more than one-half of the country’s crop.

options.label: C
options.text: Oats are more than one-third of the country’s crop.

options.label: D
options.text: The total crop of oats and wheat is greater than the corn crop.

item.figure_description:
A pie chart showing four sectors labeled with crop types:
- 'Corn': occupies slightly less than half of the circle, spanning from the 12 o'clock position clockwise to approximately the 4:30 position (roughly 135° to 140°).
- 'Oats': adjacent clockwise from Corn, spanning from approximately 4:30 to 7 o'clock (roughly 75°).
- 'Other': adjacent clockwise from Oats, spanning from approximately 7 o'clock to 8 o'clock (roughly 30°).
- 'Wheat': adjacent clockwise from Other to Corn, spanning from approximately 8 o'clock to 12 o'clock (roughly 115° to 120°).
item.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

Color of Caps

[Image: A pie chart indicating 30% white caps, 25% green caps, 15% black caps, 10% blue caps, and 20% red caps.]

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: Two graphs for the comparison of age structure between country x and country y. The x axis of both graphs shows percent of population, 0 to 8 percent, and the y-axis of both graphs is age, from 0 to 89. Each graph shows males and females separately, though the age structure is the same. Each graph indicates the proportion that are age 0 to 19, who are going to have children, those who are age 20 to 44, who are having children, and those age 45 to 89, who have finished having children. Country x age distribution shows rapid growth, where the younger ages are a greater percentage of the population than those who are older. Country y shows slow growth, where the older ages are an equal or greater percentage of the population than those who are younger. Country X has a larger percentage of people in the “having children” or “going to have children” categories than does country Y.]

The graphs for Country X and Country Y show the age structure of each country’s population. The population is divided into three age groups from youngest to oldest. The graphs enable predictions about population growth.

A. Why could the age structure of Country X lead to more rapid population growth than the age structure of Country Y?

descriptors: Within Country X there is a larger percentage of people in the “having children” or “going to have children” categories than in Country Y.
Incorrect (including crossed out, erased, stray marks, illegible, or off task)

reference_items.scoring_notes:
Note: The reference to country X needs to be clear. The comparison with Country Y does not need to be stated.
Also, accept “more people” as “proportionately more” and “young or younger” in place of “having children” or “going to have children”
Examples: Country X has more people about to have children or having children than country Y
There are more people going to have children in country X
More young people in country X

Examples:There are more “going to have children”
Country X has more population compared to country Y
reference_items.figure_description:
Two population pyramid graphs side by side under the heading "Comparison of Age Structure Between Country X and Country Y". Both graphs have a vertical axis on the left labeled "Ages" with tick marks from 0 to 89 in increments of 5 (0, 4, 9, 14, 19, 24, 29, 34, 39, 44, 49, 54, 59, 64, 69, 74, 79, 84, 89). A central vertical line divides "Males" on the left from "Females" on the right. The horizontal axis at the bottom is labeled "Percent of Population" with tick marks numbered 8 down to 0 on the left side and 0 up to 8 on the right side.

The left graph is subtitled "Country X Age Distribution / Rapid Growth". It forms a wide-based pyramid. The base (age 0) extends to approximately 7% on both the male and female sides. At age 19, it is about 3% on each side. At age 44, it is about 1.5% on each side, tapering to 0% at age 89.

The right graph is subtitled "Country Y Age Distribution / Slow Growth". It has a much narrower base and more vertical sides. At age 0, it extends to about 3% for males and 3% for females. At age 19, it is slightly below 3% on each side. At age 44, it is about 2% on each side, tapering to 0% at age 89.

Below the graphs is a key with three boxes:
- A solid dark gray box labeled "Ages 0–19 Going to have children", corresponding to the shaded bottom section (ages 0 to 19) in both graphs.
- An unshaded white box labeled "Ages 20–44 Having children", corresponding to the unshaded middle section (ages 20 to 44) in both graphs.
- A diagonally hatched box labeled "Ages 45–89 Finished having children", corresponding to the hatched top section (ages 45 to 89) in both graphs.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
Four students watched the traffic passing their school for 1 hour.

The table shows what they saw:

| Type of Vehicle | Number |
| :--- | :---: |
| Cars | 60 |
| Bicycles | 30 |
| Buses | 10 |
| Trucks | 20 |

Each student drew a graph to show the results. Which graph shows the results correctly?
reference_items.figure_description:
Four graphical representations of the traffic data:
- Option A: A vertical bar graph with the vertical axis labeled from 0 to 60 in increments of 10. The bars correspond to: Cars = 60 (solid black bar), Bicycles = 30 (light gray bar), Buses = 10 (medium gray bar), Trucks = 20 (white bar with black border).
- Option B: A pictograph with a legend stating '1 wheel = 10 vehicles'. Cars has 5 wheels, Bicycles has 4 wheels, Buses has 1 wheel, and Trucks has 2 wheels.
- Option C: A vertical bar graph with the same axis and colors as Option A, showing: Cars = 60, Bicycles = 30, Buses = 20, Trucks = 10.
- Option D: A pie chart divided into four sectors: Cars covers the right half (180°, solid black). Bicycles covers the bottom-left quadrant (90°, light gray). The remaining top-left quadrant is divided between Buses (a larger sector, medium gray) and Trucks (a smaller sector, white).
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (eighth-grade mathematics).

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem: Two-thirds of the people present at the beginning of a meeting are men. Nobody leaves but 10 more men and 10 more women arrive at the meeting. Which of the following statements is true?

options.label: A
options.text: There would then be more men than women at the meeting.

options.label: B
options.text: There would then be the same number of men as there are women at the meeting.

options.label: C
options.text: There would then be more women than men at the meeting.

options.label: D
options.text: From the information given, you cannot tell whether there would be more women or men.

reference_items.stem:
The graph shows the number of pens, pencils, rulers, and erasers sold by a store in one week.

[Image: Bar graph of items sold]

The names of the items are missing from the graph. Pens were the item most often sold, and fewer erasers than any other item were sold. More pencils than rulers were sold. How many pencils were sold?

The horizontal axis is labeled "Items Sold by Store". There are four shaded vertical bars without individual category labels beneath them. From left to right, their heights are:
- First bar: 120
- Second bar: 80
- Third bar: 140
- Fourth bar: 40

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
The results of a survey of 200 students are shown in the pie chart.

[Image: Pie chart showing popularity of rock bands]

Make a bar chart showing the number of students in each category in the pie chart.

[Image: Bar chart template]

descriptors:
All three correct - (50, 90, 60)
50 should be to the correct line.
90 should be less than 100 but greater than 80.
60 should be less than 70 but greater than 50.
Bars drawn as percentages not actual numbers
Other incorrect (including crossed out, erased, stray marks, illegible, or off task)

reference_items.figure_description:
The item includes two figures:
1. A pie chart titled "Popularity of Rock Bands" divided into three sectors: "Red Hot Peppers 25%" (shaded light gray, occupies the top-right quarter from 12 o'clock to 3 o'clock), "Stone Cold 45%" (shaded medium gray, occupies from 3 o'clock to approximately 8:30), and "Dreadlocks 30%" (unshaded, occupies from approximately 8:30 to 12 o'clock). There are tick marks on the circle edge at 12 o'clock, 3 o'clock, and 6 o'clock.
2. A blank bar chart titled "Popularity of Rock Bands". The vertical axis is labeled "Number of Students" with horizontal grid lines at 0, 50, 100, 150, and 200. Between each labeled interval of 50, there are 4 tick marks dividing each interval into five 10-unit subdivisions. The horizontal axis has three tick marks labeled "Red Hot Peppers", "Stone Cold", and "Dreadlocks".
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (eighth-grade mathematics).

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
The graph shows the time of travel by pupils from home to school.

[Image: Graph showing time of travel by pupils from home to school]

How many pupils must travel for MORE than 10 minutes?
reference_items.figure_description:
A bar graph with a vertical axis labeled "Number of Pupils" having tick marks numbered 1 through 10. The horizontal axis is labeled "Time (in minutes)" and shows four intervals:
- "0-5": bar height is 2
- "6-10": bar height is 7
- "11-15": bar height is 5
- "16-20": bar height is 2

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

location.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

guessing.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's guessing (lower asymptote) parameter c: the probability that a student of very low ability answers it correctly, such as by guessing among the options? Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.
